languages: English (international accents: Chinese, Indian and others)

links.outcome: Scribe accuracy across accents, personality styles, and speech impairments
links.effect: No significant differences across personality types (all p>0.05) or accents (patients p=0.851; doctors p=0.980); phonological impairment markedly reduced word recognition (p<0.001), while cleft palate and vowel disorders were near-perfect.
links.quote: Conversely, speech impairments differed: cleft palate and vowel disorders were near-perfect, whereas phonological impairment markedly reduced recognition (p<0.001).

links.outcome: Scribe summary errors: omissions, factual inaccuracies, hallucinations
links.effect: Omissions predominated, with low rates of hallucinations and factual inaccuracies; extraversion had highest total errors (median 3.5).
links.quote: Omissions predominated, with low rates of hallucinations and factual inaccuracies.

unlisted_practices: Predefined switch-off criteria for severe phonological speech patterns
Using synthetic voices as a proxy for accent testing

screen.reason: The study tests the robustness and error rates of an AI clinical scribe across simulated patient communication styles, accents, and speech impairments, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
